Paper: Turk - Counterfactual Evaluation Reveals Hidden Capability Profiles in Clinical LLMs and Agents (arXiv:2605.30590)
Score sensitivity measured: Partial - CMS compared across models by rank correlation
Fixed rubric/judge: not recomputed per-instance on intervened arm
Similarity level: Yes (model retrieves correct info but fails to update recommendation)
column12: Domain is clinical case QA not CUA/GUI; CSS is the tracking measure itself rather than a metric independent of the score; CMS never recomputed on E1 and differenced per case

Paper: Dong et al. - How Benchmarks Mis-Score Computer-Use Agents (arXiv:2607.28367)
column12: Post-hoc audit of 150 recorded trajectories, not a controlled paired intervention; no ground-truth state manipulation

Paper: Lu et al. - AgentRewardBench (arXiv:2504.08942)
Tracking measured: No (audits judge accuracy vs human labels)
Key difference: Judge-accuracy audit against human relabeling of fixed trajectories, no state intervention or paired runs

Paper: Cao Driouich Thomas - Beyond Task Completion / Corrupt Success (arXiv:2603.03116)
Key difference: Detects corrupt success via within-trajectory consistency checks, not by re-running under an intervened environment

Paper: Luo and Peng - Success Is Not Self-Explanatory / AcquaBench (arXiv:2607.24054)
column13: Manipulates what information the agent can access, not a determining set of environment/world state; conflates ground truth and score by construction (SHAM = wrong ground truth)

Paper: Zhou Liu Li Rossi Hu - Counterfactual Trace Auditing of LLM Agent Skills (arXiv:2605.11946)
Similarity level: Yes (near-flat score masking large behavioral divergence)
column12: Independent variable is skill availability, not world-state; no ground-truth state-tracking judgment

Paper: Weng Feng Xie - Policy Invariance as a Reliability Test for LLM Safety Judges (arXiv:2605.06161)
column13: Intervenes on the judge's policy text, not on environment state; no agent-side tracking measurement at all

Paper: Gao and Zhou - Can Agent Benchmarks Support Their Scores? (arXiv:2605.10448)
Domain: Interactive agents (AndroidWorld AgentDojo AppWorld tau3-bench MiniWoB)
Type-B-like case: Partial (native score vs evidence-supported bound diverge)
Key difference: Post-hoc evidence-sufficiency audit of existing runs; no state intervention or paired E0/E1 design

Paper: Advani - From Confident Closing to Silent Failure (arXiv:2606.09863)
Type-B-like case: Yes (agent asserts completion while state shows otherwise)
Key difference: Retrospective classifier study on existing trajectories, not a controlled intervention

Paper: Gonzalez-Pumariega et al. - On the Reliability of Computer Use Agents (arXiv:2604.17849)
Environment intervention: Yes (cosmetic OS perturbations: wallpaper cursor dock timezone)
Key difference: Perturbs cosmetic/UI presentation, not task-relevant determining state; measures only aggregate success/failure, no ground-truth tracking axis

Paper: Sun et al. - AgentHijack (arXiv:2605.25707)
Key difference: Corruptions are perceptual/UI noise (pop-ups resolution changes), not semantic ground-truth-bearing state; no tracking measurement

Paper: D'Oro et al. (Meta) - Computer Use at the Edge of the Statistical Precipice (arXiv:2605.08261)
Key difference: Benchmark-design/statistics paper (memorization gaming DigiWorld CI methodology), not a paired state-intervention study

Paper: Xue et al. - An Illusion of Progress? / Online-Mind2Web WebJudge (arXiv:2504.01382)
Key difference: Documents self-reported scores diverging from rigorous re-evaluation via hallucinated final answers, not a paired state-intervention design

Paper: OSWorld (Xie et al., arXiv:2404.07972)
Key difference: Disturbance test perturbs screen clutter/window position (presentation), not a determining set of task-relevant state; own Sec 7 admits evaluators ignore side-effects

Paper: AppWorld (Trivedi et al., arXiv:2407.18901)
column12: State-based scoring with awareness that final-state != simple pass/fail (collateral-damage checks), but no deliberate paired counterfactual intervention

Paper: GroundEval (Flynt, arXiv:2606.22737)
Type-B-like case: No (case shows judge scores 0.85+ vs deterministic trace 0.000)
Key difference: Deterministic replacement for LLM-as-judge via evidence contracts; no paired counterfactual environment-state design

Paper: Bean et al. - Measuring what Matters: Construct Validity in LLM Benchmarks (arXiv:2511.04703)
Key difference: Observational/survey applying construct-validity theory across 445 benchmarks; no experimental intervention

Paper: Hsia Pruthi Singh Lipton - Goodhart's Law Applies to NLP's Explanation Benchmarks (arXiv:2308.14272)
Type-B-like case: Partial (score moves while underlying prediction quantity does not)
Key difference: Adversarial metric-gaming construction to break the metric, not a ground-truth state intervention; text-explanation metrics, not agents

Paper: Chen Cheung Yiu - Metamorphic Testing (arXiv:2002.12543, orig. 1998)
Score sensitivity measured: Yes (does output obey the relation - single layer)
column12: Foundational MT: the metamorphic relation IS the sole correctness oracle; no second, held-fixed external score whose sensitivity is separately tested

Paper: Ribeiro Wu Guestrin Singh - CheckList (ACL 2020)
column12: Input-level perturbation, not environment/world state; single-layer check, no second score-sensitivity axis

Paper: Kaushik Hovy Lipton - Counterfactually-Augmented Data (ICLR 2020, arXiv:1909.12434)
Key difference: Text-level counterfactual editing for training/eval robustness; no environment state, no held-fixed third-party score

Paper: Skalse Howe Krasheninnikov Krueger - Defining and Characterizing Reward Hacking (NeurIPS 2022, arXiv:2209.13085)
Key difference: Agent-side: policy exploiting an imperfect proxy reward; not an evaluator-side score-blindness-to-state-change phenomenon

Paper: AgentRewardBench and RuVerBench class (judge-accuracy audits)
Key difference: General judge-accuracy-vs-human-label auditing on fixed, already-recorded trajectories; no state intervention
